### rds-proxy-multi-user-fragments-pool

**Claim.** Back-end connections are reused only for clients with the same database user name, so many unique database accounts (for example one per tenant) fragment the pool into micro-pools and reduce RDS Proxy's efficiency.

**Write it as.** `user-specific micro-pools` · `multi-user environments`

**Scope.** Amazon RDS Proxy.

> "This behavior can significantly reduce pooling and multiplexing efficiency in multi-user environments with a large number of unique database accounts."
> — [Application and workload considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-best-practices.workload-considerations.html)

> "If the database contains a thousand schemas (one per tenant) and each tenant connects to the database with a different user name, the connection pool becomes fragmented into user-specific micro-pools, reducing overall efficiency."
> — [Application and workload considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-best-practices.workload-considerations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-13.

### rds-proxy-pinning-definition

**Claim.** When RDS Proxy cannot be sure that reusing a connection outside the current session is safe, it keeps the session on the same connection until the session ends; this is called pinning.

**Write it as.** `This fallback behavior is called *pinning*.` · `keeps the session on the same connection`

**Scope.** Amazon RDS Proxy.

> "In some cases, RDS Proxy can't be sure that it's safe to reuse a database connection outside of the current session. In these cases, it keeps the session on the same connection until the session ends. This fallback behavior is called *pinning*."
> — [RDS Proxy concepts and terminology](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.howitworks.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-13.
